outcome: difficulty in delivering the fetal head
cohort: The study included 96 pregnant women with anterior asynclitism and 96 pregnant women with persistent occipital transverse position, whose clinical data was collected from January 2017 to January 2023.
finding: Age, macrosomia, obesity, pendulous abdomen, and premature rupture of membranes (PROM) were identified as independent risk factors for anterior asynclitism, which was associated with significantly higher incidences of maternal and neonatal complications compared to persistent occipital transverse position.
